result.summary: Increases the polling frequency in the Python functional test framework for node synchronization helpers and the RPC readiness wait loop. In sync_blocks and sync_mempools, the default sleep interval between checks drops from 1 second to 0.05 seconds, while wait_for_rpc_connection increases polling frequency from 4 to 20 times per second and switches to an absolute wall-clock timeout.
result.problem: Functional tests spend idle time waiting for conservative 1-second sleep intervals to elapse even when node state synchronization or RPC readiness completes in milliseconds, unnecessarily prolonging CI and local test execution times.
evidence: Author reports local test runner wall time dropped from 110.8s to 96.4s (-13%) and accumulated runtime dropped from 1715s to 1369s (-20%) on an 18-thread x86-64 machine (PR description).

Author CI runs showed test_runner.py runtime improvements across multiple environments: macOS native (-9%), 32-bit ARM (-11%), Windows native (-14%), and previous releases job (-15%) (PR description).
result.changed_since_previous: Now includes diff and CI benchmarks: wait_for_rpc_connection also replaces the iteration-count loop with an explicit time.time() wall-clock deadline.
result.card: Reduces polling sleep intervals in functional test framework sync helpers (sync_blocks and sync_mempools) from 1.0s to 0.05s, and increases RPC readiness polling from 4/s to 20/s. Tests currently waste time sleeping after operations have already finished, slowing down test runs. The author reports wall-clock reductions of 13% locally and 7% to 15% across various non-CLI CI test jobs.

risk.why: Only touches polling delays in Python functional test framework helpers; a bug could cause test flakiness or higher CPU usage during test runs.
